sources.citation: Collins, James T. 2026. Linguistic research: methods and motives. Linguistik Indonesia 44(2): 195-207. doi:10.26499/li.v44i2.1117
sources.note: No phonology (no stress/tone/accent/syllable term in the article). pp.201-202: Pusat Bahasa (Mahsun et al. 2008) classed five north-Seram languages as 'dialects' of Yamdena; quoting Collins (2019): 'The speakers of the languages in the Taniwel kecamatan, i.e. Alune, Wemale, Hulung and Naka'ela, told the Pusat Bahasa staff that they spoke different languages..'; earlier research 'summarized in Collins (2018: 73-79)'. Endnote xv quotes Mukhamdanah 2015 naming 'bahasa Hulung'. References add Collins 2019 'The Naka'ela language' (unpublished Kendari paper) and Collins 2020 'Krisis di Indonesia Ti…

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste. Berlin: Language Science Press (langsci 526).
sources.note: Nothing for Hulung. Sec. 10.4.1 (p.437): 'Hulung [huk] *b > p; *mb/*mp > k; **au > oi'; Appendix A.7: sole Hulung data source is Collins 1983. (The only prosodic remark nearby concerns Alune's extrametrical -e, not Hulung.)

sources.note: Nothing. pp.155-156: 4-5 speakers aged 60+ in 1978 (quotes Collins 1982:102 and Collins 2018a:78); 'provided at least 1500-1700 lexemes and phrases as well as recorded stories' (unpublished field data); endnote xxvii: S. Touwe p.c. 2016 reports speakers still exist.

sources.citation: Mukhamdanah. 2015. Bahasa Yamdena di Maluku: korespondensi, variasi dialektal, dan sebaran wilayah pakainya [Yamdena language in Moluccas: the correspondence, dialectal variation and its area distribution use]. Widyaparwa 43(1): 39-54. Yogyakarta: Balai Bahasa DIY.
sources.note: Nothing on stress or tone (a full-text search for stress/accent tekanan|aksen|nada|stres|suku kata|prosodi = 0; sec. 2.2.2 states all four change types treated 'merupakan perubahan bunyi yang bersifat segmental'). Hulung-specific content is segmental: p.43 'Hal ini ditunjukkan bahwa [p] pada dialek Hulung selalu muncul sebagai [b] pada dialek Alune' (glosses tangan, sungai, hapus); '[k] pada dialek Nakaela dan dialek Alune selalu muncul sebagai [0] pada dialek Waemale Utara dan dialek Hulung'; p.44 '[ma] pada dialek Hulung selalu muncul sebagai [m] pada dialek Nakaela dan selalu muncul [0] pa…

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 2003. Language death in Maluku; the impact of the VOC. Bijdragen tot de Taal-, Land- en Volkenkunde 159(2/3): 247-289.
sources.note: Open-access at Brill but could not be reached by automated download; historical sociolinguistics of Seram language loss, may mention Hulung; very unlikely to state stress.

sources.citation: Holton, Gary. 1996. Bibliography of language and language use in North and Central Maluku (Southeast Asia Paper 40). Honolulu: Center for Southeast Asian Studies, University of Hawai'i. 95 pp. hdl:10125/19366
sources.note: Pointer only: the single Hulung source it knows is [81] 'COLLINS, JAMES T. 1976. Field Notes in Languages of Indonesia. ms. Unpublished wordlists and grammatical notes for languages of Central Maluku.. Length of individual lists varies from 100 to 500 words, and many lists include grammatical annotations. Includes lists for.. Seram Laut (3 dialects), Hulung, Latea, Luhu, Hoamoal (Luhu, Piru)..'. Confirms that as of 1996 no published or archived description of Hulung existed beyond Collins's notes.

sources.citation: Taguchi, Yushin. 1989. Lexicostatistic survey of the languages indigenous to West Seram. In Wyn D. Laidig (ed.), Maluku (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 6), 15-63. Ambon: UNPATTI-SIL.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 4.3.1.4: 'HULUNG, spoken by fewer than ten people in the village of that name and its hamlet Sauweli, is nearly extinct'; SIL survey wordlist (H. Wemale, 7/9/85, Taguchi) unpublished; lexicostatistic percentages only.
sources.venue: Maluku (Workpapers in Indonesian Languages and Cultures 6)

sources.citation: Collins, James T. 1983. The historical relationships of the languages of Central Maluku, Indonesia. Pacific Linguistics D-47. Canberra: ANU. ix+168 pp.
sources.note: Nothing for Hulung. Hulung ('never before mentioned in the extant literature', p.40; 3-4 surviving speakers; informants M. Wemale, E. Neuwe) appears only in comparative sound-change tables (loini, poini, soi, toini, lau; asa, malapa, manuala, sipa, nia; pulane, pusule, papu, patu) and the Ulat Inai subgrouping argument (*b > p, loss of *-w). Forms carry no stress marks. The book's only explicit stress-placement rule concerns Hoamoal vs Asilulu (pp.82-83).
